placements.title: Technology stack swaps ratified through quantified performance-cost math
placements.frame: What performance or cost figure is being used to justify replacing one system with another, and what tradeoffs (migration risk, data integrity, downtime) does that framing leave unstated?
placements.why: src-1 announces a settled decision to replace PostgreSQL with QuantumDB; src-2 supplies the unhedged performance/cost rationale (10x query performance, lower licensing cost) immediately backing it; src-3 is an independent summary that restates the same migration, the same performance figure, and adds a Q3 2026 timeline as settled fact. The specific PostgreSQL/QuantumDB swap is a one-time fact and does not itself become a leaf (grain test) — but the pattern it evidences, technology decisions settled and justified by a quantified performance/cost figure, is a subject future envelopes (other stack swaps, other vendor decisions) are likely to keep feeding. No existing graph structure or strata was supplied to reuse against, so this is a NEW standalone mint with nothing close enough to lineage against.
